name: Empagliflozin

lead: Empagliflozin is a prescription tablet that lowers blood sugar by making the kidneys excrete glucose in urine. It is approved for type 2 diabetes, heart failure and chronic kidney disease.

Its appearance angle is body composition: the calorie loss through urine produces modest weight loss in trials, which some people interested in fat loss discuss. Trials reported about 2% of baseline body weight lost on average, and a systematic review placed it in the mild weight-loss group.

paras: It is taken by mouth under medical supervision for its approved conditions. Off-label use for appearance is discussed in some communities but is not a recognised indication.

Documented risks include genital fungal infections, low blood pressure, and rare but serious ketoacidosis, including with normal blood sugar, and Fournier's gangrene. It is prescription-only and not recommended in pregnancy.

forums.title: E2 Not Responding to Arimidex, Aromasin

chain: Calories lost as glucose in urine
angle.text: Empagliflozin's weight effect is modest, around 2% in trials, which is why it appears in discussions of fat loss. Its approved uses are medical.

lead: Empagliflozin, sold as Jardiance, is a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor developed by Boehringer Ingelheim and co-marketed with Eli Lilly. It was approved in the EU in May 2014 and in the US in August 2014 for type 2 diabetes, and later for heart failure and chronic kidney disease.[1]

For looks, the relevant effect is weight: by blocking glucose reabsorption in the kidney it causes calorie loss in urine, and trial participants lost about 2% of baseline weight on average.[1] A systematic review of antidiabetic drugs classed empagliflozin among agents with mild weight loss, below 3.2% of initial weight, compared with stronger effects from semaglutide and tirzepatide.[2]
Large trials have studied it in cardiovascular, heart-failure and kidney populations.[3][4][5] It is a prescription drug and has no approved cosmetic use.

paras: It improves glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes, reduces cardiovascular death in adults with diabetes and heart disease, treats heart failure, and slows kidney decline, including in people without diabetes.[1][3][4][5]
The weight loss seen in trials is the link to appearance. Reviews of antidiabetic drugs and weight place it in the mild category.[2]

Common effects are genital fungal infections, low blood pressure and nausea. Serious but rare effects include diabetic ketoacidosis, which may occur at normal blood glucose, and Fournier's gangrene. Use in pregnancy and breastfeeding is not recommended.[1]
A pooled safety analysis of four large trials (about 10,000 patients on empagliflozin) found similar rates of serious and fatal adverse events versus placebo.[6]
It inhibits SGLT2 in the proximal tubule, reducing glucose reabsorption; it is the most selective of the marketed SGLT2 inhibitors.[1]

EMPA-REG OUTCOME reported cardiovascular outcomes and mortality in type 2 diabetes.[3] EMPEROR trials examined heart failure, and EMPA-KIDNEY examined chronic kidney disease.[4][5] A network meta-analysis compared glucose-lowering drugs across 453 trials.[7] A systematic review compared their weight effects.[2] No trial has tested empagliflozin as a cosmetic weight-loss treatment in people without these conditions.

timeline.event: Approved in the EU (May) and US (August).[1]
